title: Stand in for the host so client tests run offline

blocks.text: A client test that needs a real host is slow, depends on a network, and cannot make the host decline on demand. Everything the client does passes through its `MUX`, so the client can be tested against a stand-in that answers in the same process, the way the host would, and whose answers the test controls.
Write `SimulatedHost`, a jPOS `MUX` built from an amount limit in minor units (cents). Its `request(ISOMsg request, long timeout)` answers at once with a reply that:

items: has the response MTI of the request (`0100` is answered with `0110`, `0800` with `0810`);
echoes every field the request carried;
sets field 39 to `51` (insufficient funds) when the amount in field 4 is over the limit, and to `00` otherwise.

blocks.text: The other `MUX` methods: `isConnected()` is always true, `send` accepts a message and answers nothing, and the asynchronous `request` hands the same reply straight to the listener.

items: The reply is a new message. The client still holds its request, and a test may still check it, so answering must not change it.
A request that carries no amount, such as a network echo test, is approved.

cases.says: a request within the limit is answered with the response MTI, its own fields echoed and response code 00
a request whose amount is over the limit is answered with response code 51
answering leaves the client's own request message unchanged
a request that carries no amount, such as an echo test, is approved
